questions.question_text:
During Prim's algorithm, the vertices currently in the tree are $\{A, B\}$.
The candidate edges to unvisited vertices are $AC=6, AD=4, BC=5, BD=7$.
Which edge is selected next?

options.why: Chose the lowest-weight edge connected to the last added vertex $B$ only (greedy path error).
Selected the first alphabetical edge instead of the lowest weight.
Selected the highest-weight available edge instead of the lowest weight.
Included heavy edge $EF=8$ instead of the lighter tree connection $CE=6$.
Summed all edge weights in the entire network.
Omitted the edge needed to connect vertex $D$.
Used $BC=13$ instead of $DC=11$, giving the incorrect known-edge total $33$ and $k=38-33=5$.
Used $FA=12$ instead of $FB=7$, giving the incorrect known-edge total $36$ and $k=38-(5+12+8+11)=2$.
Omitted $DC=11$ and vertex $C$, subtracting only $5+7+8=20$ from $38$.

questions.solution_text:
Begin with the given MST edge $EF$. Add $FB=7$, $BA=5$, $ED=8$, then $DC=11$, choosing the lowest-weight edge to an unvisited vertex each time.
The MST edges are $EF, FB, BA, ED, DC$.
$k+7+5+8+11=38$
$k=38-31=7$.
With $k=7$, Prim's algorithm starting at $A$ selects $AB, BF, FE, ED, DC$, confirming the total.

questions.question_text:
The table gives the edge weights of a connected network. Use Prim's algorithm starting at $X$ to find the total weight of the minimum spanning tree.
$\begin{array}{c|ccccc}&U&V&W&X&Y\\\hline U&-&27&14&16&18\\V&27&-&21&23&25\\W&14&21&-&29&17\\X&16&23&29&-&20\\Y&18&25&17&20&-\end{array}$

options.why: Used $UY=18$ instead of $WY=17$, adding $1$ to the minimum total.
Used $XV=23$ instead of $WV=21$, adding $2$ to the minimum total.
Selected all four edges from $X$, giving $16+23+29+20=88$, instead of checking edges from all vertices currently in the tree.

questions.solution_text:
Start at $X$ and choose $XU=16$.
From $X$ and $U$, choose $UW=14$.
From $X, U, W$, choose $WY=17$.
Finally choose $WV=21$ to connect $V$.
The MST edges are $XU, UW, WY, WV$.
$\text{Total weight}=16+14+17+21=68$.
